contract.label: Alert
contract.summary: The one tinted callout: a box laying out an optional icon, AlertTitle, AlertDescription, and a top-right AlertAction. Any tinted message with an icon and a title is this component, never a hand-built subtle-tinted box.
contract.purpose: The one tinted callout. Any message in a tinted box with an icon and a title — a notice, a warning, an error, a confirmation that stays on the page — is this component, so every callout in the product reads the same and adapts to dark on its own.
useWhen: A message belongs to the content it sits beside and stays until the condition clears — a meter offline, a tariff change coming, a reconciliation done.
The message carries a status: the tone says what kind of thing happened before the title is read.
dontUseWhen: The message is page-wide and above the content — that is `banner`.
The message is transient confirmation of an action — that is `toast`.
Nothing has happened; the box would only decorate a paragraph.

parts.name: Alert
parts.description: Root callout container with role=alert and variant styling.

parts.name: AlertTitle
parts.description: Bold heading text for the alert. A long title wraps rather than truncating.

parts.name: AlertDescription
parts.description: Secondary descriptive body text below the title.

parts.name: AlertAction
parts.description: Top-right slot for a dismiss or action button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Tone: default, destructive, success, warning, or info. A status tone tints the surface with the status colour and sets the text to its -emphasis token — the only text colour on a tint.

requires: A title; a description where the title alone does not say what to do.
A status `variant` chosen by meaning — `destructive` only for an error, `warning` for a condition to act on, `info` for a notice, `success` for a done thing.
forbids: A hand-built callout — a `div` with `bg-warning-subtle`, an icon and a bold line. It is this component.
Text on a tint in any colour but the tone's `-emphasis` token: never the base fill colour, never `foreground` on a status tint.
A coloured strip along an edge to signal the status — the tint and the icon carry it.
rules: **Any tinted callout with an icon and a title is `Alert`**, never a hand-built `bg-*-subtle` box. The component tints the surface, draws the icon in the tone and sets the text to the tone's `-emphasis` token — the only text colour on a tint.
Status tones are picked by meaning, as everywhere: `destructive` is an error, `warning` a condition to act on, `info` a notice, `success` a done thing.

behavior.error: An error that has a retry carries it in `AlertAction` or in the description, so the alert is not a dead end.

requirements: The root carries `role="alert"`; a message that is not an interruption and only informs may be given `role="status"` instead.
The tone is never the only signal: the title says what happened in words.

examples: `<Alert variant="warning"><TriangleAlertIcon /><AlertTitle>Approaching demand threshold</AlertTitle><AlertDescription>Meter MTR-4471-0092 is at 94% of the 1,200 kW monthly peak.</AlertDescription></Alert>`
antiPatterns: A `div className="bg-warning-subtle rounded-lg p-3"` with an icon and a bold title — a redrawn `Alert`, which will drift from the real one on the next token change.
`text-warning` or `text-foreground` on a warning tint — text on a tint is `text-warning-emphasis`.
